payload.headline: Small dip; SPY and QQQ hold long trends but stay below 50-day averages

summary.thesis: Both indices sit between their trend lines. They are above their 200-day averages, so the long trend holds. They are below their 50-day averages, so the short trend is broken. Fear reads normal, but only 25% of stocks are above their 50-day averages.
summary.decision: Selective for long-term buyers. Stand aside for swing setups until QQQ closes above its 50-day average.
summary.act_at: QQQ close above 718.46 (50-day average) or SPY close above 764.43 (50-day average) to lean in more. SPY close below 728.99 or QQQ close below 680.94 (200-day averages) to stand aside.

payload.happening: As of Nov 12, SPY closed at 757.12, down -0.35% on the day. QQQ closed at 688.17, down -0.32%. This was a quiet giveback after the prior session's bounce. Over 5 days both are up: SPY 3.29% and QQQ 6.35%. Over 20 days both are still down: SPY -1.9% and QQQ -5.47%. Both indices set their 1-month low closes on Nov 5, at 733.00 for SPY and 647.05 for QQQ, and have rebounded since. They remain short of their 1-month highs: 773.09 for SPY on Oct 21 and 728.00 for QQQ on Oct 15. The past year's highest closes were 779.09 for SPY and 759.66 for QQQ, both on Oct 6. The data shows no news since the last note. No market gate is active.
payload.business: Trend: both indices are labeled sideways. Each is above its 200-day average, so the long trend holds. Each is below its 50-day average, so the short trend is broken. QQQ is 4.4% below its 50-day and SPY is 1.0% below its own, so tech is further from repairing its short trend. Fear: the VIX reads 'normal' (the 15–20 band), at the 56th percentile of its past 252 readings. That reading is from Nov 11, because the Nov 12 value isn't stored yet. Breadth: 25% of stocks are above their 50-day averages. (General knowledge: breadth shows how many stocks take part in a move. A low reading means most stocks have not joined the bounce.) Together, the readings show no panic and an intact long-term trend. The recent rebound is narrow, though, and the short-term trend is not yet repaired. That mix tends to suit choosing individual names over buying broadly.

worth.text: This is a market-level note, and DATA contains no valuation inputs. The levels cited are trend references, not estimates of worth.
worth.key_assumption: No valuation is implied. The levels are price-trend markers only.

bull: Both SPY and QQQ remain above their 200-day averages (728.99 and 680.94), so the long-term trend counts as up.
Over 5 days, SPY is up 3.29% and QQQ is up 6.35%. Both are well above their Nov 5 lows of 733.00 and 647.05.
Fear is in the 'normal' band (56th percentile), not elevated or high.
bear: Both indices are below their 50-day averages (SPY 764.43, QQQ 718.46), so the short-term trend is broken. QQQ is 4.4% below its line.
Breadth is weak: only 25% of stocks are above their 50-day averages.
On a 20-day view, QQQ is down -5.47% and SPY -1.9%. Both remain below their 1-month highs, so the pullback is not recovered.

levels.what: SPY 50-day average: a close above it would put SPY's short-term trend back up.
SPY 1-month high (Oct 21): a close above it would mean SPY's pullback is fully recovered.
QQQ 50-day average: a close above it would put the short-term trend back up and pass the pipeline's market check. That would be the cue to lean in more.
QQQ 1-month high (Oct 15): a close above it would mean the tech pullback is fully recovered.
SPY 1-month low (Nov 5): a close below it would set a new 1-month low, meaning the decline is continuing.
SPY 200-day average: a close below it would put the long-term trend down. That would be a stand-aside signal.
QQQ 200-day average (QQQ is 1.1% above it): a close below it would put tech's long-term trend down. That would be a stand-aside signal.
QQQ 1-month low (Nov 5): a close below it would mean the tech decline is continuing.

longterm.why: The long-term trend holds and fear is normal, which argues against standing aside. The broken short-term trend and 25% breadth argue against leaning in broadly. Together they favor only the strongest names over broad buying.

swing.why: QQQ closed at 688.17, below its 50-day average of 718.46. Per the trend gates, setups keep failing the pipeline's market check until QQQ closes above that level.

decision.timing: PPI comes out Nov 13 at 08:30. It is an early read on inflation pressure. NVDA reports earnings on an estimated Nov 17, after the close. Per DATA, its big index weight means the report moves the whole tech group. Both events are close enough to push the indices toward or away from the gate levels. The VIX reading is from Nov 11, and the Nov 12 value isn't stored yet.

change_mind: Toward lean in: QQQ closes above 718.46 (its 50-day average), which passes the pipeline's market check, and SPY closes above 764.43. A close above the 1-month highs (QQQ 728.00, SPY 773.09) would mean the pullback is fully recovered.

Toward stand aside: SPY closes below 728.99 or QQQ below 680.94 (the 200-day averages), which would put the long-term trend down. Closes below the 1-month lows (SPY 733.00, QQQ 647.05) would mean the decline is continuing.
payload.what_changed: The previous note (Nov 11) covered a strong bounce day. Nov 12 was a small down day: SPY -0.35% and QQQ -0.32%. The verdict is unchanged: long trend intact, short trend broken, breadth 25%. The moving gate levels drifted. SPY's 50-day went from 764.55 to 764.43, QQQ's 50-day from 718.87 to 718.46, SPY's 200-day from 728.65 to 728.99, and QQQ's 200-day from 680.65 to 680.94. QQQ's 1-month high reference changed from 728.95 (Oct 14) to 728.0 (Oct 15). The data shows no new news.
